## claude.ai HyperFrames by HeyGen

[HeyGen HyperFrames MCP] — Programmable HTML video projects.

## When to use this MCP

This MCP is the primary HyperFrames surface for hosted chat clients (Claude.ai
web/desktop, ChatGPT, Grok, and similar), where the user has no local filesystem
and the agent cannot author HyperFrames code directly.

From a CLI/IDE agent on the user's machine (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, the
localhost MCP Inspector, etc.), **`compose` and `render_video` are disabled** — these clients have a local
filesystem, so author HyperFrames with the local HyperFrames skills instead, which
produce standalone HTML compositions the user can edit, diff, and commit. Calls to
those two tools from such clients are rejected with a pointer to install them:

    npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes

The read tools (list_projects, get_project, get_project_status, get_render_status)
stay available to every client.

After installation they expose slash commands like `/hyperframes` (compose),
`/hyperframes-cli` (init, lint, preview, render), and `/hyperframes-media`
(TTS, transcribe, remove-background). See
https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes for the full skill list and docs.

But the skills and this MCP are *not* drop-in equivalents:

- Local skills → standalone HTML/GSAP files on disk. No `project_id`, no hosted
  artifact, no integrated cloud render pipeline.
- This MCP → hosted HeyGen project with a `project_id`, a live canvas at
  `app.heygen.com/projects/{id}`, and the cloud render queue.

Route by what the user actually wants:
- "Make a local HTML composition / something I can edit" → use a local skill.
- "Make a HeyGen project I can share / render in the cloud / open in the app"
  → use this MCP, even from a CLI agent.

## What it does

HyperFrames is HeyGen's framework for creating, editing, and rendering programmable
HTML-based video projects. Projects are authored interactively (Magic Edit
chat-driven flow) and rendered to MP4, WebM, or MOV at any framerate. Tools exposed
here cover composing, listing, fetching, and rendering projects… [truncated]

# Handoff — 2026-09-15 — Technology inventory refresh

## What was worked on, and why

Eric downloaded a newer Microsoft Forms responses file for the Athletics
Technology Inventory. The job: pull it in, compare it with the previous run
(2026-08-29 export), and update the inventory reports. Done on the Baylor
Windows laptop; the refresh branch was merged to `main` (refresh commit
`baafe4a`, STATUS commit `7a6ed7d`).

## Result

- 51 submissions (up from 37). None of the 37 earlier responses changed.
- 31 of 32 units answered for themselves. **Volleyball's only entry is a
  Business Office vendor list** — its own staff have not answered.
- 185 products (+38), 75 athlete-data candidates, 120 single-unit, 9 retirements
  (new: Cizr, Constant Contact).
- Full write-up: `docs/FINDINGS_2026-09-15.md`.

## Decisions made, and the reasoning

1. **Business Office entries are tagged, not merged into unit responses.** One
   Business Office respondent entered 12 responses (Baseball 8/20, Football 8/28,
   ten on 9/14) — vendor lists from purchasing/contract records, plus the Business

def main():
    master, long, long_all, cov_all, stopped, unmapped, prose = load()
    by = {r["canonical"]: r for r in master}

    def units(name):
        return int(by[name]["unit_count"]) if name in by else 0

    cov = [r for r in cov_all if r["unit"] not in PHANTOM_UNITS]
    units_total = len(cov)
    units_self = [r for r in cov if r["status"] in ("responded", "MULTIPLE")]
    bo_only_units = [r["unit"] for r in cov if r["status"] == "BUSINESS OFFICE ONLY"]
    no_response = [r["unit"] for r in cov if r["status"] == "NO RESPONSE"]

    n_sub = len({r["response_id"] for r in long_all}
                | {r["response_id"] for r in stopped}
                | {r["response_id"] for r in prose})
    n_products = len(master)
    n_athlete = len([r for r in master if r["athlete_data_likely"] == "Y"])
    n_single = len([r for r in master if int(r["unit_count"]) == 1])
    n_mentions = len(long)
    n_excluded = len(long_all) - len(long)

    bo_rows = [r for r in long_all + stopped if r.get("source") == "business-office"]
    n_bo_entries = len({r["response_id"] for r in bo_rows})
    # The Business Office's own department-wide list is not a list "for" a unit.
    bo_units = sorted({r["unit"] for r in bo_rows} - {"Business Office"})
    bo_only = [r for r in master if r.get("unit_count_self_reported") == "0"]

    in_use = {}
    for r in long:
        if r["status"] == "in_use":
            in_use.setdefault(r["canonical"], set()).add(r["unit"])
    planned = [r for r in long if r["status"] == "planned"
               and r["unit"] not in in_use.get(r["canonical"], set())]

    deck = ("{} submissions across the department, and a second view from the "
            "Business Office's records. Most of the technology here still sits "
            "with a single unit.".format(n_sub))
    d = BaylorDoc(TITLE, deck=deck, status=STATUS)

    d.meta([
        ["Status", "**Interim** — collection stays open to the department "
                   "soft deadline of September 29, 2026"],
        ["Date", long_date(EXPORT)],
        ["Source", "Microsoft Forms — Quick Inventory (5 questions), responses "
                   "workbook as of {}".format(long_date(EXPORT))],
        ["Previous run", "Export of {}".format(PREVIOUS["date"])],
        ["Prepared by", "Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics"],
        ["Companions", "Athletics Technology Inventory — Executive Summary "
                       "(one page); Technology Lists"],
    ])

    d.callout(
        "What changed since {}".format(PREVIOUS["date"]),
        "**{} new submissions**, and none of the earlier {} was changed or "
        "withdrawn. Tennis (M), Tennis (W) and Golf (M) responded for "
        "themselves. On September 14 the Business Office entered vendor lists "
        "from its purchasing and contract records for nine sport units, "
        "including Volleyball, whose own staff have not yet answered, and a "
        "department-wide list of its own. Products named "
        "rose from {} to {}, and retirements from {} to {}."
        .format(n_sub - PREVIOUS["submissions"], PREVIOUS["submissions"],
                PREVIOUS["products"], n_products, PREVIOUS["retired"], len(stopped)))

    # --- 1 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("At a glance — where the inventory stands")
    d.table(
        ["Measure", "Now", PREVIOUS["date"].split(",")[0], "Note"],
        [["Submissions", n_sub, PREVIOUS["submissions"],
          "{} of them entered by the Business Office".format(n_bo_entries)],
         ["Units answering for themselves",
          "{} of {}".format(len(units_self), units_total),
          "{} of {}".format(PREVIOUS["units_self"], units_total),
          "Volleyball is covered only by the Business Office's list"
          if bo_only_units else "Interim"],
         ["Distinct products", n_products, PREVIOUS["products"],
          "Resolved from {} separate mentions".format(n_mentions)],
         ["Products touching athlete data", n_athlete, PREVIOUS["athlete"],
          "{}% of products, by category — a screening list".format(
              round(100 * n_athlete / n_products))],
         ["Products used by a single unit", n_single, PREVIOUS["single"],
          "{}% of products".format(round(100 * n_single / n_products))],
         ["Retired in the last 12 months", len(stopped), PREVIOUS["retired"],
          "Vendor data disposition not recorded"]],
        widths=[1.9, 0.75, 0.85, 3.2], numeric_cols=(1, 2))
    d.small("Units are counted out of {}: the form listed 33 options, and "
            "“Other” was never selected.".format(units_total))

    # --- 2 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Coverage — who has responded")
    d.para("**{} of {} units have answered for themselves.**".format(
        len(units_self), units_total)
        + (" {} {} covered only by the Business Office's vendor list, so the "
           "unit's own view of what it uses is still to come."
           .format(" and ".join(bo_only_units),
                   "is" if len(bo_only_units) == 1 else "are")
           if bo_only_units else "")
        + (" Still to respond: {}.".format(", ".join(no_response))
           if no_response else ""))

    d.subhead("Units that submitted more than once")
    multi = [(r["unit"], r["unit_responses"]) for r in cov if r["status"] == "MULTIPLE"]
    d.para(", ".join("{} ({})".format(u, n) for u, n in multi) + ".", space_after=4)
    d.para("These are different people describing different slices of the same "
           "unit. They are kept and tagged rather than merged. Business Office "
           "entries are counted separately and are not included here.")

    d.subhead("Coverage by unit")
    rows = []
    for r in cov:
        own, bo = int(r["unit_responses"]), int(r["business_office_entries"])
        label = {"responded": "Responded", "MULTIPLE": "{} people".format(own),
                 "BUSINESS OFFICE ONLY": "Business Office list only",
                 "NO RESPONSE": "Not yet in"}.get(r["status"], r["status"])
        rows.append([r["unit"], own, bo or "", label])
    d.table(["Unit", "Unit responses", "Business Office", "Status"], rows,
            widths=[2.9, 1.1, 1.1, 1.6], numeric_cols=(1, 2))

    # --- 3 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("A second source — the Business Office's records")
    d.para("The Business Office submitted **{} entries**: vendor lists for **{} "
           "units** — Baseball and Football in August, the rest on September 14 "
           "— and a department-wide contract list of its own. They are drawn "
           "from purchasing and contract records rather than describing "
           "day-to-day use."
           .format(n_bo_entries, len(bo_units)))
    d.para("That makes them the cross-check the previous report recommended. "
           "Every row in the data now records whether a unit named a product "
           "itself or it came from the Business Office, so the two views can be "
           "read side by side. Where they differ, neither is wrong: a contract "
           "shows what is paid for, and a unit's answer shows what is used.")
    d.para("Products named by more than one unit through the Business Office "
           "include Hudl ({} units, {} by the unit itself) and DVSport ({} units, "
           "{} by the unit itself)."
           .format(units("Hudl"), by["Hudl"]["unit_count_self_reported"],
                   units("DVSport"), by["DVSport"]["unit_count_self_reported"]))

    d.subhead("Products known only from the Business Office's lists")
    d.table(["Product", "Category", "Listed for"],
            [[r["canonical"], pretty(r["category"]), r["units"]]
             for r in sorted(bo_only, key=lambda r: (r["category"], r["canonical"]))],
            widths=[2.2, 1.6, 2.9])
    if "Recovery Record" in by:
        d.para("**Recovery Record** appears only here. It is an eating-disorder "
               "treatment app, so it holds athlete health information, and no "
               "unit named it. It belongs at the front of the detailed second "
               "pass.", space_before=3)

    # --- 4 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("The estate — most of it sits with one unit")
    d.para("{} of {} products were named by a single unit. That long tail — not "
           "the vendor overlap — is the finding. It is the population no "
           "central process currently sees.".format(n_single, n_products))
    d.para("It includes AI tools adopted locally (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, "
           "Microsoft Copilot, Grammarly), a scatter of productivity and "
           "communication apps (Notion, Asana, Todoist, Padlet, Sling, GroupMe, "
           "Jotform), and one-off athlete-facing systems (Nix Biosensors, Calera "
           "CORE, Boost Treadmills, C3 Logix, Hologic DXA, Foresight GCQuad, "
           "Edgertronic).")

    d.subhead("Distinct products by category")
    cats = {}
    for r in master:
        cats[r["category"]] = cats.get(r["category"], 0) + 1
    d.table(["Category", "Products"],
            [[pretty(k), v] for k, v in sorted(cats.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1])],
            widths=[3.0, 1.0], numeric_cols=(1,))

    d.subhead("Products used by three or more units")
    d.table(["Product", "Units", "Named by the unit", "Category"],
            [[r["canonical"], int(r["unit_count"]),
              int(r["unit_count_self_reported"]), pretty(r["category"])]
             for r in master if int(r["unit_count"]) >= 3],
            widths=[2.3, 0.7, 1.4, 2.3], numeric_cols=(1, 2))
    top = max(master, key=lambda r: int(r["unit_count"]))
    d.para("**{}, at {} units, is the only thing close to a department-wide "
           "system.** Everything below it is departmental at best."
           .format(top["canonical"], top["unit_count"]), space_before=3)

    # --- 5 -----------------------------------------------------------------
    d.section("Overlap — several vendors, one job")
    d.para("The consolidation conversation is answerable with counts rather than "
           "estimates. One new overlap arrived with this export: **Hawkin "
           "Dynamics**, a force plate system, which the Business Office listed "
           "for Volleyball, alongside VALD elsewhere in the department.")
    n_video = len([r for r in master if r["category"] == "video-analytics"])
    d.table(["Job", "Vendors in use (units)"],
            [["Athlete tracking",
              "Catapult ({}), Kinexon ({}), Polar ({}); Firstbeat arriving".format(
                  units("Catapult"), units("Kinexon"), len(in_use.get("Polar", ())))],
             ["Force & speed testing",
              "VALD ({}), Perch ({}), GymAware ({}), Hawkin Dynamics ({}), TMG ({})"
              .format(units("VALD"), units("Perch"), units("GymAware"),
                      units("Hawkin Dynamics"), units("TMG"))],
             ["Athlete management",
              "Teamworks ({}), Kitman Labs ({}), XPS Network ({})".format(
                  units("Teamworks"), units("Kitman Labs"), units("XPS Network"))],

STATUS = "Interim — collection open to September 29, 2026"

TEXT_WIDTH = 6.7        # Letter less the house 0.90in side margins
SHOW_CHECKLIST = False  # dropped in Eric's 09-01 edit

# "Other" was an option on the form that nobody ever selected, and it looks
# like a leftover from the draft list. It is not a unit that owes a response.
PHANTOM_UNITS = {"Other"}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# data
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def figures():
    def rd(name):
        with open(os.path.join(CLEAN, name), encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return list(csv.DictReader(f))

    long_all = rd("tech_inventory_long.csv")
    master = [r for r in rd("tech_master.csv") if r["category"] != "excluded"]
    long = [r for r in long_all if r["category"] != "excluded"]
    stopped = rd("stopped_using.csv")
    prose = rd("prose_responses_review.csv")
    cov = [r for r in rd("coverage.csv") if r["unit"] not in PHANTOM_UNITS]

    units_total = len(cov)
    units_self = [r["unit"] for r in cov if r["status"] in ("responded", "MULTIPLE")]
    bo_only_units = [r["unit"] for r in cov if r["status"] == "BUSINESS OFFICE ONLY"]
    no_response = [r["unit"] for r in cov if r["status"] == "NO RESPONSE"]

    n_products = len(master)
    n_athlete = len([r for r in master if r["athlete_data_likely"] == "Y"])
    single = [r for r in master if int(r["unit_count"]) == 1]
    single_units = {r["units"] for r in single}
    top = max(master, key=lambda r: int(r["unit_count"]))

    # Every submission leaves a trace in one of these three files.
    n_sub = len({r["response_id"] for r in long_all}
                | {r["response_id"] for r in stopped}
                | {r["response_id"] for r in prose})

    bo_rows = [r for r in long_all + stopped if r.get("source") == "business-office"]
    bo_only_products = [r["canonical"] for r in master
                        if r.get("unit_count_self_reported") == "0"]

    return dict(
        units_total=units_total, n_units_self=len(units_self),
        bo_only_units=bo_only_units, no_response=no_response,
        n_outstanding=len(bo_only_units) + len(no_response),
        n_sub=n_sub, n_mentions=len(long), n_products=n_products,
        n_athlete=n_athlete, n_single=len(single), n_single_units=len(single_units),
        top_name=top["canonical"], top_units=int(top["unit_count"]),
        n_stopped=len(stopped),
        n_bo_entries=len({r["response_id"] for r in bo_rows}),
        # The Business Office's own department-wide list is not a list "for" a unit.
        n_bo_units=len({r["unit"] for r in bo_rows} - {"Business Office"}),
        n_bo_only_products=len(bo_only_products),
        bo_health="Recovery Record" in bo_only_products,
    )


def plural(n, one, many):
    return one if n == 1 else many


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the document, as data
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
def content(f):
    """Everything the reader sees. Both renderers consume this and nothing else.

    ** ** marks inline bold in every string.
    """
    if f["bo_only_units"]:
        gap = ("{}, whose own staff have not yet answered"
               .format(" and ".join(f["bo_only_units"])))
    else:
        gap = None

    brief = ("Every unit was asked to complete a five-question survey naming the "
             "technology it uses. **{n_units_self} of {units_total} units** have "
             "answered, describing **{n_products} products**. ".format(**f))
    if f["n_bo_entries"]:
        brief += ("The Business Office also entered vendor lists from its purchasing "
                  "and contract records for {n_bo_units} units".format(**f)
                  + (", including {}".format(gap) if gap else "") + ". ")
    brief += ("Collection stays open to September 29. The full list of products in "
              "use and products retired in the last 12 months is a separate document.")

    if f["n_outstanding"]:
        still = ", ".join(
            ["{} (Business Office list only)".format(u) for u in f["bo_only_units"]]
            + f["no_response"])
    else:
        still = "None"

    rows = [
        ["Units that have responded",
         "**{n_units_self} of {units_total}**".format(**f)],
        ["Units still to respond", still],
        ["Submissions received", "**{n_sub}**".format(**f)],
        ["Distinct products named", "**{n_products}**".format(**f)],
        ["Products that likely involve athlete information",
         "**{n_athlete}**".format(**f)],
        ["Products named by one unit only", "**{n_single}**".format(**f)],
        ["Most widely shared system",
         "**{top_name}**, listed by {top_units} different units".format(**f)],
        ["Products retired in the last 12 months", "**{n_stopped}**".format(**f)],
    ]
    if f["n_bo_entries"]:
        rows.append(["Products known only from Business Office records",
                     "**{n_bo_only_products}**".format(**f)])

    takeaways = [
        "**Most products have a single user.** {n_single} of the {n_products} "
        "products were named by only one unit each, spread across "
        "{n_single_units} different units.".format(**f),
        "**One system is close to department wide.** {top_name}, at {top_units} "
        "units.".format(**f),
        "**{n_stopped} products were retired in the last year.** What each vendor "
